newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ terms of trade deteriorate in Dec qtr.
newsitem.headline: NZ terms of trade deteriorate in Dec qtr.

text.p: New Zealand's terms of trade fell by 1.5 percent from the September 1996 quarter to the December 1996 quarter, Statistics New Zealand said on Tuesday.
"After declining throughout most of 1996, the terms of trade index is now 3.5 percent lower than in the December 1995 quarter," SNZ said.
"The terms of trade index is, however, 8.7 percent higher than the average level during the 1980s."

Dairy prices fell by 4.7 percent in the latest quarter and have weakened during the last three successive quarters. Other contributors to the latest fall in export prices included forestry products, meat, machinery and transport equipment, wool, fish and aluminium.

Export volumes in the December 1996 quarter were 9.8 percent higher than a year ago. Over this period, dairy volumes increased 32.8 percent while forestry products rose 15.2 percent. In the latest quarter, export volumes were 5.3 higher than the September quarter level, however, SNZ said this movement was affected by seasonal influences.
